text: Original promotion gate: spread-model expectancy with day-clustered 95% lower bound > 0; out of sample on a window fixed before the test, >= 150 trades over >= 3 months; beats a random-entry baseline (5 draws from a committed contract-day list) by more than one round-trip cost; fills validated against captured NBBO, edge must survive the adverse fill model; look-ahead audit on file; reproducible from committed artifacts. Never promote on mid-only profit, CIs including zero, operator P&L, in-sample results, < 150 trades.
status: superseded by GATE-v2 for lane classification; items retained

text: Six gates, every applicable one must pass: data integrity (full chains incl. extreme-move days, hashed); execution realism (bid/ask at measured NBBO, fees, official settlement, every assumption stated); statistical validity (positive net expectancy, day-clustered 95% lower bound > 0 on complete data, out of sample, after multiplicity accounting); tail survival (stated loss under worst historical intraday move and ±10%/±15% shocks, capital so the stress loss stays within budget, Reg-T and portfolio margin); forward validation (>= 150 sessions AND >= 7 calendar months of forward paper trading with live NBBO logging); product classification (signal lane must also beat random entry by > one round trip; carry lane need not, and must be labelled carry). Win rate is reported, never a gate.

GeorgeFi's history is evidence about GeorgeFi's record, not about Compass hypotheses. A GeorgeFi number may motivate a hypothesis; it never counts toward promoting one. Owner's decision 2026-10-14: GeorgeFi reverse-engineering is no longer an objective; its data and execution-cost findings are preserved for reuse.

family: baseline signal validity on the underlying (no options)
method: signed underlying return (direction x return, bp) 5/15/30/60 min after the decision bar and to the close, and 15/30 min before it; random-minute controls matched by symbol/date/direction (5 seeds, uniform in the entry window); component ablations; day-clustered 95% CIs
verdict: The baseline entry rule has no forward predictive value on index ETFs over nine years and selects worse minutes than random (signal minus random about -6 to -8 bp over 30 minutes): it fires after a local move (+10 to +14 bp in the prior 30 minutes). Diagnosis for S01: no directional edge / late entry, not costs. No component ablation produces a positive forward return.

family: entry triggers on the underlying (rsi_cross, vwap_reclaim, ema_cross_5m, breakout_5m, retest_5m, trend_pullback, bounce) × filter sets (raw, baseline_filters, confirm_5m, align_15m)
method: signed underlying return after the decision bar at 5/15/30/60 min and to close; pre-signal 15/30 min; matched random minutes (same symbol/date/direction, 5 seeds); day-clustered 95% CIs (1,000 draws); entry window minutes 15-320
promotion_rule: absolute lower bound at 30 or 60 min >= +3 bp AND paired lower bound vs matched random > 0 (two-part rule adopted after this screen: see 05_results.md S06)
verdict: No entry trigger on the index ETFs carries a forward move after the decision bar: every raw trigger sits within about +/-1 bp of zero at 30 and 60 minutes over nine years (73k RSI crosses, 27k VWAP reclaims, 5.5k 5-minute EMA crosses, 5.5k breakouts, 4.7k retests, 5.7k trend pullbacks, 10k bounces per symbol). The baseline filter stack lowers every trigger relative to random (breakouts and retests by -14 to -21 bp at 60 min, the RSI lead by -10 to -14 bp) because it fires after +20 to +38 bp of prior movement. The bounce trigger beats its matched random control by +4 to +11 bp only because the control inherits the day drift against the counter-trend direction; its absolute forward return is zero (-0.3 to +0.6 bp at 30 min), so a long option bought on it would pay the full cost for no expected move. Nothing is promoted to an option test on index ETFs; the screen moves to the Tier A single-name universe (S05 bars).

family: daily triggers for the Weekly/Swing/Position categories (gap_cont, breakout20, reversal5, trend_pullback, event_shock) × (raw, relvol>=1.5)
window: 2024-01-02..2026-10-13 (2023 for the point-in-time universe and warm-up)
instruments: every optionable root with prior-calendar-year median daily dollar volume >= $50M, >= 200 bars and median price >= $5 (1,119 / 1,210 / 1,510 symbols in 2024 / 2025 / 2026); stock EOD lake data_lake/thetadata/stock_eod
method: signed return from the next session open to the close 1/5/10/21 sessions later, absolute and minus the same-date eligible-universe mean in the trigger direction; CIs clustered by event date (1,000 draws); pre-registered in 04_protocol.md A2 with hurdle abs lower bound >= +30 bp at 5/10/21 AND adjusted lower bound > 0
verdict: No daily trigger is promoted. Breakouts (112,938 events) and trend pullbacks (45,185) are followed by underperformance, not continuation: breakout20 -31 bp at 5 sessions [-54, -9], -81 at 21 [-133, -33], adjusted -47 [-81, -14]; trend_pullback -33 at 10 [-67, -3], adjusted -97 at 21 [-141, -55]; negative in each of the three years. Gap continuation, 5-day reversal and volume/return shocks (the earnings proxy) have CIs that include zero at every horizon with year signs that flip. Exploratory, not pre-registered: the inverse of breakout20 (fade) would clear the absolute part of the hurdle only at 21 sessions (+81 [+33, +133]); in option terms a 0.5-delta long option on a 60-DTE single-name contract would earn about 40 bp of spot from that move against roughly 110 bp of theta over 21 sessions and 40 bp of spread (C1 half-spreads), so it is not a long-option edge; it could only be carried by a short-premium or spread structure, which is outside the long-option scope until the owner decides.

family: Earnings/Events at daily resolution: direction = EPS surprise sign (entry at the event open = gap, or the next open = drift) and direction = event-day move (drift entry); cells by surprise tercile, report time, agreement of the move with the surprise
instruments: S07 point-in-time universe (prior-year median $ volume >= $50M); 10,439 quarterly reports with EPS, estimate and report time on 1,186 symbols over 594 event dates (5,745 pre-market)
method: as S07 (same-date universe mean adjustment, CIs clustered by event date, 1,000 draws); pre-registered as 04_protocol.md A3; hurdle as A2
verdict: Nothing promoted. 77 % of reports beat the estimate, so the surprise-sign direction is mostly long and its absolute returns (+30 bp at 10 sessions [+8, +54], +68 at 21 [+35, +99] from the event open; top-tercile beats +79 / +132) are the 2024-2026 market drift: adjusted for the same-date universe they are negative (-17 [-35, +3] at 10, -31 [-59, -2] at 21; drift entry -25 [-39, -9] and -44 [-70, -17]; top-tercile beats after the first day -86 [-136, -39] at 21). Post-market reports are worse than pre-market. Direction = the event-day move carries nothing (-5 [-23, +13] at 10 sessions); moves that disagree with the surprise reverse weakly (+19 [+2, +36] at 5 sessions adjusted, absolute negative). No post-earnings drift in the surprise direction exists in this universe and window at 1-21 sessions; beats are sold after the gap.

verdict: The 10-session pre-earnings run-up clears the A2 underlying hurdle (absolute lower bound >= +30 bp and adjusted lower bound > 0) with the same sign in every year; 5 sessions clears the adjusted part only (+52.9 [+22.4, +81.6]; adj +23.3 [+10.3, +35.1]). It earns an option test (A5.2): the expression must carry a 10-session hold against theta, so it is a long call or straddle bought 10 sessions before and sold at the pre-event close, where the pre-event implied-volatility rise is the other half of the P&L; chains per event are being pulled with S11.

method: amendment A5 (underlying part of S16); 108 cells; CIs clustered by date
verdict: Nothing promoted. Gap continuation and gap fade are both indistinguishable from zero at every horizon on all three ETFs. Fading the prior session close-to-close move has 6 of 108 cells with a positive 95 % lower bound (2.7 expected by chance), the largest QQQ on |gap| >= 0.5 % days held to the next close: +17.8 bp [+4.7, +30.2], hit 52 %, negative in 2017 only; the others are +5 to +12 bp with 1-5 negative years. verdict: Nothing promoted. Walk-forward out of sample (2024-2026): lower-bound objective -$3.81 [-5.23, -2.35] (n 3,200), mean objective -$3.94 [-6.11, -1.80], expected-profit/worst-drawdown objective -$2.49 [-7.32, +2.46] (selects invalidation_only every year; 2026 +4.94 [-6.11, +16.27] on 432 trades is the only positive fold and its interval includes zero). The grid confirms S04: the sign is set by the entry, and no period, threshold, filter, delta band, spread limit, stop, target or hold changes it.

family: direction after entries and day selection, cross-referenced against ThetaData minute bars and 0DTE chains
instruments: SPY, QQQ, IWM, SPXW (ETF proxies for the index underlying)
verdict: Epoch 1 shows a directional and day-selection edge (+12.5 bp at 15 min, hit 71 %; +$48/contract over random days) that is inseparable from the same rows' fills-better-than-market anomaly (G1); Epoch 2, the epoch recorded under live conditions, has no directional information at any horizon (−0.6 bp at 15 min, hit 52 %; −2.4 bp vs random at 30 min) and no day-selection edge on ETF roots. The record offers no entry rule; the exit layer is its only robust component and it reduces losses rather than creating expectancy.
